message.content: {"calls": [{"tool": "chest_xray_classifier", "source_filename": "figures/734/figure_1.jpg", "reason": "To obtain normalized scores for consolidation, opacity, and other parenchymal patterns to support the assessment of airspace disease distribution."}, {"tool": "chest_xray_report_generator", "source_filename": "figures/734/figure_1.jpg", "reason": "To generate a natural language description of the opacities, specifically looking for mentions of peripheral, subpleural, or migratory consolidations characteristic of COP, which helps distinguish between central vs. peripheral distribution options."}], "reason": "The question requires identifying the specific pattern (central vs. peripheral) and distribution (upper vs. lower/middle) of airspace consolidation to diagnose Cryptogenic Organizing Pneumonia (COP). The classifier will provide quantitative evidence of consolidation presence, while the report generator is critical for describing the morphological location (e.g., 'peripheral', 'subpleural') that differentiates COP from other etiologies like pneumonia or edema. Both tools are necessary to resolve the ambiguity between options A/B (central) and D (peripheral)."}
